findings.title: T2 is the only tier with a clean record so far
findings.body: T2: 4 targets, 0 stops, 2 still open. T1: 3 targets, 18 stops. T3: 0 targets, 5 stops. T3 also has 3 open and 2 unclear.

findings.title: T2 is 6 alerts, and 3 of its wins are one USDJPY rally
findings.body: The three USDJPY buys on 9 Nov are one move counted three times. Without them T2 is one win (AUDJPY sell, 13 Nov) and two open sells. Do not call T2 the best signal until it has 20 or more alerts across different days and symbols.

findings.title: T1 buys all lost in one falling week
findings.body: All 15 decided T1 buys were stopped, and all but one were 16 to 19 Nov, when USD and JPY were strong. T1 is meant to fire against the MAs, so in a strong trend it fires into the trend. This says T1 buys lost in this week, not that T1 never works.

findings.title: T1 and T2 and T3 are not independent
findings.body: A T2 or T3 alert follows an EDGE EXH on the same symbol. They are often the same setup seen at different times, so the tiers should be compared per setup, not as separate trades.

findings.title: Scoring is not the same for every row
findings.body: T1 log rows count as stopped if price touched the stop before the opposite alert, with no time cap. T2, T3 and the 3 screenshot T1 sells were read from price on the chart. Some stops and targets in the screenshots were hard to read.

findings.title: Does a T2 after a T1 beat the T1 alone?
findings.body: For each setup, compare the T1 entry with the T2 or T3 entry that followed on the same symbol. If the later entry wins more often, the cross is worth waiting for. Needs more pairs.

findings.title: T1 in the direction of the 4H trend versus against it
findings.body: Add the 4H trend state at each alert and compare. This is the check that would explain the T1 buys.

findings.title: Trend Gate CAUTION
findings.body: 6 of the 20 log T1 alerts carry CAUTION (5 stopped, 1 open). Too few, and non-CAUTION alerts also lost. Keep recording it.

After the Plus chart export, rescore every alert from exact prices so all rows use one method.
method: Only confirmed 4H alerts (T1 = EDGE EXH confirmed, T2 = MA cross, T3 = PC cross). Each alert is scored from its own entry, target and stop: which was touched first. Target is about 2.3 to 3 times the stop. A win counts as the target distance in R, a loss as minus 1R. Open and unclear alerts are left out of the win rate and the average R. Sources: Discord alert screenshots (6 to 20 Nov) for T2 and T3 and for 3 T1 sells, and the TradingView alert log for 20 T1 alerts (16 to 19 Nov).
